transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

That burning rubber smell is a big clue. It almost always means the drive belt has slipped, stretched or snapped, usually because the brush bar got jammed with hair or something got caught. Suction through the hose still working confirms the motor is fine. It's just the brush not being driven.

Unplug it first.

### 1. Check for a jam
• Flip the vacuum over and look at the brush bar.
• Cut away any wrapped hair, thread or carpet fibres (scissors or a seam ripper work well).
• Check the ends of the brush bar too, as hair loves to wind into the bearings there.
• Try spinning the brush by hand. It should turn freely.

### 2. Check the belt
• Remove the base plate (usually a few screws or clips on the underside).
• Look at the rubber belt running from the motor spindle to the brush bar:
• Snapped or missing: needs replacing
• Loose, shiny, melted or cracked: needs replacing
• Fine but slipped off: clear the jam, refit it, and test

### 3. Check the brush bar switch/setting
Some Vax models have a brush on/off button or a carpet/hard floor setting. Make sure it's set to carpet/brush on. Some also have a reset button or thermal cut-out that stops the brush if it jams. Check your manual for this.

### Getting a replacement belt
• Find your model number on the sticker on the back or underside of the machine.
• Search "[model number] belt". They're cheap (usually a few pounds) from Vax's website, Amazon, eBay or appliance spares shops.
• Some Vax uprights (e.g., certain Mach/Air models) use a geared belt or clutch rather than a simple rubber band. Matching the model number makes sure you get the right one.

### If the belt's fine and nothing's jammed
Some newer Vax models have a separate small motor inside the brush head instead of a belt. If that's burnt out, you'd need a replacement brush bar/motor assembly. It's worth checking the price against the cost of the machine.

If you tell me the model number, I can help narrow down exactly what you need.

model is U85-AS-Be, its a Vax Air Stretch. just had a look, brushbar was tight w loads of hair and a tassel round the ends, cut it all off n it spins free now. belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit looks melted on the edge

Snapped and melted is exactly what happens when the brush bar jams. The motor keeps spinning the belt against a stuck pulley until the friction burns through it. You've already done the hard part by clearing the jam, so you just need a new belt.

### Getting the right belt
• Search "Vax U85-AS-Be belt" or "Vax Air Stretch belt" on the Vax website, Amazon, eBay or a spares site like eSpares.
• Check the listing specifically says it fits the U85-AS range, since Vax uses different belts across models.
• Genuine Vax belts are a bit dearer but tend to last longer. Packs of 2 are handy so you have a spare.

### Before fitting it
• Clean off melted rubber. Check the motor spindle (the small metal shaft the belt loops round) and the pulley on the brush bar. Any melted residue will make the new belt slip or wear fast. Scrape it off gently, then wipe with a cloth and a bit of isopropyl alcohol if you have it.
• Check the brush bar ends. Pull off the end caps if they come off and remove any hair still wound round the bearings or axle. A tassel jam often leaves fibres hidden there. If a bearing feels gritty or rough when you spin it, that can cause the next belt to fail too.
• Look for damage. Make sure nothing's cracked or melted on the plastic housing near where the belt runs.

### Fitting
1. Loop the belt round the motor spindle first.
2. Stretch it over the brush bar pulley, then seat the brush bar back into its slots.
3. Spin the brush by hand to check the belt runs straight and doesn't rub on anything.
4. Refit the base plate, then test on carpet.

A new belt will feel quite tight. That's normal.

### Preventing it happening again
• Cut hair off the brush bar every few weeks, more often with long hair or pets.
• Lift the head or switch the brush off when going over rugs with tassels or fringes.
• If you smell burning rubber or hear the brush slow down, switch off straight away. Catching it early can save the belt.
